page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng benchmarks, while single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average capabilities. However, multi-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10%, and uncached large block read and write bandwidths falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile, the n2d-highmem-2 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing or high-speed local storage. It is poorly suited for database operations, Redis deployments, and static web serving, which all scored in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Instead, this instance is best utilized for lightweight memory-bound applications, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic administrative workloads that benefit from a dedicated AMD EPYC core and a larger memory footprint relative to compute capacity.
